Subject: Re: DPA redline: residency and erasure windows

Maya —

Thanks for the redline and the clear deadline. We reviewed the document with our legal and infra teams this morning. We understand Solera's priority is: (1) EU-only processing for customer PII, (2) a firm delete/erase guarantee after termination, and (3) assurance that backups won't be retained beyond the stated window.

High-level reply / Redwood counterproposal:
- Residency: Redwood can commit to processing and storing Solera-controlled content in EU regions by default for this account (we will route primary inference and storage to our Frankfurt and Amsterdam clusters). We will document the region routing in the SOW and allow an onshore-only processing flag.

- Deletion windows: we cannot accept a blanket 180-day deletion across all system copies without carving for standard operational backups / recovery. Proposed compromise: 
  * Customer data (customer-created content, prompt/response records, embeddings) — delete or render unrecoverable within 30 days of confirmed termination for all live stores.
  * System backups and disaster-recovery copies — retention up to 90 days maximum, with a contractual commitment to accelerate deletion where feasible and to provide an explicit deletion certificate once complete. Backups are immutable for short windows to allow recovery from corruption; 90 days is our limit.
  * Audit logs and telemetry (operational logs that may include hashed identifiers) — retain up to 180 days for security/incident investigation; we can scope which logs contain customer-identifiable content.

- Key control and encryption: we propose optional BYOK for keys (customer-managed KMS) so Solera can independently revoke keys after termination, which would render backups cryptographically inaccessible before physical deletion completes.

Next steps: I want to align internally on the exact redline text for the DPA before we send a formal counter. Looping in Neha (privacy counsel) and Vanessa (customer success lead) to sign off. If Solera prefers the 180-day hard cap for all copies, that is a commercial/legal escalation and would likely require a separate carve-out and additional indemnities/insurance.

If it helps, we can provide a SOC2-Type II summary and a proposed DPA paragraph set.

Best,
Karthik

Requested input:

In particular, confirm we can commit to certifying deletion of backups within 90 days and provide a deletion certificate. Also confirm whether the BYOK revocation approach is reasonable as a mitigation.
- Vanessa: confirm operational impact and what we can promise in terms of deletion certificate delivery timelines (we typically provide evidence in 10–14 business days after deletion completes). Also advise whether enabling EU-only routing for this account requires any additional capacity reservations.

Upon termination of services, Redwood will delete or render unrecoverable Customer Content stored in primary systems within thirty (30) days. Redwood will delete backup and disaster-recovery copies within ninety (90) days; where technical immutability prevents immediate deletion, Redwood will make commercially reasonable efforts to accelerate deletion and, upon completion, furnish Customer with a deletion certificate. Backups are immutable for short windows to allow recovery from corruption; 90 days is our limit.
  * Customer data (customer-created content, prompt/response records, embeddings) — delete or render unrecoverable within 30 days of confirmed termination for all live stores.
  * System backups and disaster-recovery copies — retention up to 90 days maximum, with a contractual commitment to accelerate deletion where feasible and to provide an explicit deletion certificate once complete. Backups are immutable for short windows to allow recovery from corruption; 90 days is our limit.
  * Audit logs and telemetry (operational logs that may include hashed identifiers) — retain up to 180 days for security/incident investigation; we can scope which logs contain customer-identifiable content.

- Key control and encryption: we propose optional BYOK for keys (customer-managed KMS) so Solera can independently revoke keys after termination, which would render backups cryptographically inaccessible before physical deletion completes.

Next steps: I want to align internally on the exact redline text for the DPA before we send a formal counter. Looping in Neha (privacy counsel) and Vanessa (customer success lead) to sign off. To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 19 Jan 2026 16:42:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Internal: Solera DPA redline — proposed language and asks

Karthik / team —

Thanks for the clear draft. Legal has reviewed and we can sign off on the compromise with two small edits to tighten assurance for Solera while keeping reasonable operational limits:

1) Change the "delete or render unrecoverable within thirty (30) days" language for primary systems to read: "within thirty (30) days following Customer's written notice of termination or expiration, Redwood will take commercially reasonable steps to delete or render unrecoverable Customer Content in production systems and notify Customer when deletion is complete." This clarifies the trigger and adds notice.

2) For backups: keep the 90-day maximum, but we will add language that Redwood will maintain a documented backup schedule with retention buckets and will, upon request, provide the applicable retention bucket for Solera within five (5) business days. We will also commit to providing a deletion certificate within fourteen (14) business days after physical removal is completed.

BYOK: we can offer the BYOK option but cannot treat key revocation alone as a contractual replacement for physical deletion in all cases. We can include language that key revocation renders copies inaccessible and that Redwood will still follow the 90-day removal process for physical copies; however, we will treat a customer key revocation as immediate evidence of customer intent to render data inaccessible and will expedite physical deletion where possible.

I recommend we send the revised text (below) to Solera with the SOC2 summary and the erase_matrix.xlsx attached. Vanessa, please confirm we can include the EU routing SOW note and whether this requires a soft capacity reservation. Rishi, add any operational caveats you need in the final paragraph.

Revised paragraph for DPA: 
"Redwood will, by default, store and process Customer Content for the Solera account within the European Economic Area (EEA). Upon Customer's written notice of termination or expiration, Redwood will take commercially reasonable steps to delete or render unrecoverable Customer Content in production systems within thirty (30) days and shall notify Customer when deletion is complete. Backup and disaster-recovery copies shall be deleted within ninety (90) days; Redwood shall maintain documentation of backup retention buckets and shall provide Customer with the applicable retention bucket for Solera upon request within five (5) business days. Upon completion of physical removal of backup copies, Redwood will provide Customer a deletion certificate within fourteen (14) business days. Audit logs that contain Customer Identifiers may be retained for up to one hundred eighty (180) days for security and incident response purposes. Customer may elect to use Customer-managed encryption keys ("BYOK"). Revocation or destruction of such keys by Customer shall render copies inaccessible and Redwood will treat such revocation as evidence of Customer's intent to render Customer Content inaccessible and will use commercially reasonable efforts to expedite physical removal; notwithstanding the foregoing, Redwood's obligations to physically remove copies remain subject to the ninety (90) day backup removal window."

Please let me know if any of you object to this language; otherwise I'll send to Solera this afternoon with the SOC2 summary and the erase_matrix.

-Neha
